content: Dicloxacillin is an antibiotic that can cause liver damage, also known as hepatotoxicity. If you experience symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, fever, weakness, unusual fatigue, itching, loss of appetite, light-colored stools, dark-colored urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), contact your healthcare provider immediately. Individuals allergic to dicloxacillin or any of its ingredients should not take this medication. Your pharmacist can provide a complete list of ingredients in the specific dicloxacillin product you are prescribed. Dicloxacillin should be taken on an empty stomach with a large glass of water (at least 4 ounces or 120 milliliters), either one hour before or two hours after a meal. Remain upright (sitting or standing) while taking the medication and avoid lying down or taking it right before bed. Only take dicloxacillin if it has been prescribed to you by a healthcare provider, and follow the prescribed dosage. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have similar symptoms, as it may harm them. Keep dicloxacillin out of reach of children. Before starting dicloxacillin, inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions, as well as any prescription or over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are using. This will help determine if dicloxacillin is appropriate for you. Dicloxacillin may interact with other medications, so it is important to discuss any potential interactions with your healthcare provider, especially if you are taking tetracyclines, probenecid, or warfarin. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider, as the effects of dicloxacillin on pregnancy and the unborn baby are not well understood. Similarly, if you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, let your healthcare provider know, as dicloxacillin passes into breast milk. Dicloxacillin is best absorbed on an empty stomach. While it is unclear if alcohol affects dicloxacillin, heavy drinking can weaken your immune response and make it harder for your body to fight infections. If you accidentally take too much dicloxacillin, seek medical help immediately by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Complete the full prescribed course of dicloxacillin, even if your symptoms improve, to reduce the risk of antibiotic resistance. Common side effects of dicloxacillin include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and a black hairy tongue. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Serious side effects, though less common, include severe allergic reactions, antibiotic-associated diarrhea, seizures, kidney damage, and blood disorders. If you experience symptoms such as difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, hives, severe diarrhea, blood in your stool, muscle twitching, confusion, reduced urination, or unusual bruising, stop taking dicloxacillin and seek immediate medical attention. Dicloxacillin is available in 250 mg and 500 mg oral capsules. Store it at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C) and protect it from extreme temperatures.
